A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work despite the changed title and formatting. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original fine-tuning experiments, normalization and momentum analyses, quadratic simulations, and nanoGPT training results.

after.justification: V5 retains these original empirical results and adds real-model weighted-Hessian estimates and gradient-sign reliability measurements.

M1.justification: The optimizer definitions and SignSGD (S) scaling are retained. Appendix H extends theoretical analysis to existing block-normalization methods; it does not establish a changed proposed or experimentally implemented optimizer.

E1.justification: Both versions cover the same nine fine-tuning datasets, nanoGPT training on Shakespeare, and homogeneous and heterogeneous quadratic problems. The new diagnostics use existing models and tasks.

E2.justification: The empirical optimizer comparisons, including momentum variants and SignSGD (S), are retained. No-LN remains in the appendix normalization comparison. SCALE is newly discussed but is not empirically evaluated.

E3.justification: Sections D.1–D.2 add evaluation procedures for batch-aggregated weighted-Hessian quantities and sampled-coordinate sign mismatch. The existing dataset splits, model configurations, and hyperparameter tables S.1–S.4 remain unchanged; additional training runs are not established.

E4.justification: V5 adds real-model weighted-Hessian comparisons and a direct check of the new sign-reliability condition. These extend the existing correlation and quadratic analyses. Normalization, scheduler, momentum, attention, and other supplementary analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table S.6 adds a 90th-percentile summary of batchwise sign mismatch alongside its mean. Existing five-seed reporting, standard deviations, and interquartile training-curve bands remain unchanged; no increased run count is stated.

E6.justification: New Tables S.5–S.6 report real-model curvature and sign-mismatch estimates. For example, pre-trained RoBERTa/RTE has weighted-Hessian estimates 52.6 and 2.28, while its mean sign mismatch is 0.429. Existing accuracy, Gini, nanoGPT, quadratic results, and plotted data are preserved.

T1.justification: V5 introduces additive noise floors, a weighted sign-reliability assumption, and substantially revised stochastic bounds and proofs. V3's noise-adapted Appendix G bound is generalized into Theorem 4.9, while its original relative-noise SignSGD bound is retained as Corollary A.3. New Appendices G and H derive common-l2 and block-normalized complexity bounds.

C1.justification: V5 explicitly frames the analysis around fine-tuning and SignSGD as a tractable proxy for Adam-like behavior, narrowing v3's more direct explanation of Adam. The central gradient/Hessian heterogeneity and Post-LN contributions remain.

C2.justification: V5 replaces the suggestion that noise dependence is relatively minor with explicit sign-reliability and noise-floor qualifications. It adds common-norm and block-partition limitations, qualifies the Post-LN mechanism, and revises SGD's alleged failure on RoBERTa to task-dependent slower convergence, acknowledging CB's similar final losses.

D1.justification: Sections D.1–D.2 document the new estimators, batch aggregation, and checkpoint selection. Section C.1 specifies that clipping at 1.0 applies to SGD. Hardware, existing training settings, dataset statistics, and hyperparameter disclosures are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: V5 adds Glentis et al. (2025) and connects SCALE and other block-normalization methods to the theoretical framework. Table 1 changes Crawshaw et al. (2022) and Kunstner et al. (2024) from partial to full Transformer coverage. Other cited works are retained.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, contribution statements, and selected explanatory passages are rewritten, including Sections 4.6–4.7 and 5. Appendix organization and cross-references are updated, but the broad narrative order and most existing appendix prose remain.

P2.justification: The main text changes from two-column formatting to a single-column journal layout, with extensive figure and table repositioning. Figure 3's ViT panel moves to Figure S.6, Table 2 drops a duplicated No-LN row retained in the appendix, and two diagnostic tables are added. Underlying plots are unchanged.

improvement.justification: V5 improves claim calibration and adds useful diagnostics and a common-norm comparison. However, its theoretical expansion introduces unresolved proof gaps: A.4 Eq. (13) bounds the parameter-weighted additive-noise term using ΛG without establishing ΛP ≤ ΛG, and H.1's descent argument does not control the δD B term under its stated δD < ΛBN/3 assumption. These affect the claimed extensions beyond v3. The explanatory and empirical gains coexist with substantive theoretical concerns, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
